chapter: Harry James, Bellson and the return to Duke
title: Duke repeatedly asks him to return
summary: Even after he left, Duke asked him to come back, even just to hold his horn on the stand, and Juan always refused.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Duke tried to get you to come back and play again, even after you quit for the last time?
Oh yeah, he was always making cracks about -- "When you gonna bring your trombone?"
And every time he'd come to town, he would come to the house and ask Juan, "What do you want me to give you for you to come back with the band?" And Juan would say, "I don't want to go back with it."
But you see, if he had treated Juan right in the first place, he would have kept Juan. Juan would have

never left him to go with Harry James, because Juan is true at heart, you know what I mean? When Juan promises you something, you can bet your bottom dollar that he is going to do it if he can, do you understand what I'm saying?

Uh huh. Well, I remember when you were working with Duke after you had left the band, you'd be extracting, and Duke would be recording them and he used to ask you to come play on the recording dates. You never would.
And he used to ask you to play just while the band was in town; he knew you wouldn't go on the road, but would you just play the local dates -- and you would never do it.

And he told Juan one time, 'Just sit up there and hold your horn,' and Juan said, 'I can't do that.' Do you remember, Juan? He told Juan, he said, 'Just sit up there and hold your horn,' and Juan said, 'I can't do that; I can't be supposed to be playing and not playing.'
Yeah, he wanted me to do that. I said, 'How can I be on the bandstand holding my horn?'
He told him to travel with him, you know; not to play, and he said, 'I'll pay you -- just sit there and hold your horn.' Oh, he begged Juan to come back to him many, many times.
And every time he'd come to town, he would come right to this house.
Yeah, he did some bad things for me, but he was a nice fellow, too.
I could get every- anything I wanted from him.
After Juan showed him that he meant business, you know. Because, after all, music is a business.
You can't get friendship and business mixed up together, you know.
